meanings: The reviewer discovered Softwear through an influencer recommendation.
During the first few months, the reviewer loved Softwear and considered it the best lip balm they had used.
While using Softwear, the reviewer woke with substantial dead lip skin and had to rub or brush it off every morning; they speculated this meant Softwear was doing its job.
The reviewer liked Softwear's very thick consistency and sheen, while also reporting resistance when rubbing lips together and accommodating by avoiding that action.
After several months, the reviewer developed what they describe as perioral dermatitis, rough lips, and tiny lip bumps, severe enough to obtain prescribed steroid cream.
After recovery, the reviewer retried Softwear hoping something else had caused the dermatitis; their lips flared within 24 hours, worse than before, and they concluded Softwear caused it.
The reviewer had three unopened tubes stocked from the favorable months, considered about CAD 70 wasted after the reaction, and was devastated because they loved the product.
The reviewer considers Softwear reasonably priced, still recommends trying it, but cautions people with sensitive lips.
The reviewer had never previously experienced a reaction like this or considered their lips sensitive.
The reviewer considers other people's tolerance unpredictable, has read other reviews criticizing Softwear consistency, partly understands that criticism, and envies people who can use Softwear.
limitations: Medical causality is the reviewer's conclusion only, without independent medical confirmation. Other-review consistency criticism is attribution or echo, not verified separate observations.
